fields.name: CUSTOMEREDUCATION1

CUSTOMER EDUCATION If BT Cloudphone's integrated voice response is not recognizing the DTMF codes that the phone is sending, the issue is likely isolated to the carrier or the phone sending the codes. Refer the customer to their respective carrier to isolate the problem. Issue is not with BT Cloudphone Probe if the customer has any other unresolved issues. Take ownership and appropriate action to ensure unresolved issues are handled correctly.
  • Inform the customer that the issue is isolated to the carrier and that the incident could simply be a simple isolated failure on their system.
  • Inform the customer to contact us right away in the event of a recurrence.
  • Re-use the guide in the event that the customer has another call forwarding failure involving another user or call forwarding medium.
  • Do not forget to select the correct Call Handling Disposition based on how you handled the problem.
Recommended Dispositions:
  • Call Forwarding - Agent Turned On/Off Settings

fields.fieldText:
Ensure that the DigitalLine number is working. Ask the customer what the DigitalLine number is then dial the number directly from inContact. Successful test calls should do any of the following:
  • Ring to the phone with no connection error.
  • Connect to the phone and be able to talk to a live person.
Unsuccessful test calls may do any of the following:
  • Connect to a "Not in service" message or something similar.
  • Ring to a busy tone.
  • Play no audible message or tone indicating that the phone number is working.
Additional Steps: Check porting ticket If number the was ported recently check if the porting request was completed on the same day. If happens on the same day, Consult with NTD for the activation timeline. If not, refer to BT- mobile,landline,business,voip (carrier/owner). Note: In the event that you get mixed results (successful AND unsuccessful), the test calls should be considered unsuccessful.

fields.name: IdentificationoftheCallForwardingproblembasedonunsuccessfultestcalls
fields.fieldText:
Identification of the Call Forwarding problem based on unsuccessful test calls. If the customer is still experiencing issues receiving forwarded calls, "Session Log" will tell you why call forwarding is not working.
  • Ask the customer for the phone number where the call came from as well as the date and time of when the call was placed.
  • Search for that call in "Session Log"
  • Note that "Session Log" show all logs in Pacific Time, so if you need help converting the time, please use available online tools such as:
    • Time Difference Calculator
    • Time Zone Converter
Analyzing results from "Session Log" Below are the components to look for when analyzing issues involving call forwarding:
  • Blue: Caller information
    • This indicates the number of the caller. The phone number is under "Caller ID".
    • This component is categorized under "Session Type" as "Caller".
  • Red: Callee information
    • This indicates the number that was dialed as well as the extension which routed the call.
    • This component is also categorized under "Session
    • Type" as "Caller".
  • Yellow: "Find Me" status
    • This indicates the number where the call was routed to. The number is under "Called number".
    • The result of the call routing is shown under the column: "Action".
    • This component is categorized under "Session Type": "Find me".
  • Green: Call leg information
    • All calls that show on "Session Log" are grouped into "Legs" shown under "Session ID".
    • Each leg determines what happened during a particular call, from the time the call started, to the time the call ended.
    • "Session ID" is unique for each and every call through RingCentral.
The sample above indicates the following facts:
  • The caller's number is 33153676674.
  • The BT phone number dialed is 442072211133.
  • The user extension the call was routed to was handled by user extension 306.
  • The call was routed to a non-BT number 447083003436.
  • The call was successfully answered by the non-BT forwarding number.

fields.name: UnderstandingthedifferentFindMeStatuses
fields.fieldText:
Understanding the different "Find Me" Statuses "Caller Hangup" generally indicates that the caller hung up before the callee answered the call. "Answered - Not Accepted" indicates that the call has been forwarded and picked up by the callee, however RingCentral did not recognize that the callee "accepted" the call by pressing "1". Pressing "1" is an option triggerred by enabling the "Incoming call information" feature called "Play announcement before connecting". "Call Succeed" indicates that the callee successfully answered the call. "Time out" generally indicates that the "Ring for" duration was exceeded without the callee answering the phone. "Force stopped" is generally the same as "Time out" however it is triggered if there are multiple forwarding numbers involved within the answering rule. It indicates that the system "forces" the call fowarding to "stop" when the set "Ring for" duration was exceeded. Below are some of the network connectivity issues that may cause problems with call forwarding to DigitalLine numbers.
  • Poor internet service directly affects SIP registration and signaling. IP telephony devices configured to connect to BT Cloudphone are registered to BT using an internet connection. Problems with the internet connection should be handled accordingly by the internet service provider.
  • Incorrectly configured network source. A network source that is not configured to work with VOIP will affect SIP registration and signaling. It is best to configure the modem or router to allow connections to and from BT Cloudphone using BT Broadband Capture Strategy
  • Unsupported IP telephony device. Features that are not working on unsupported devices that were never tested by BT Cloudphone should be referred to their respective manufacturers.
Powercycle the IP telephony device to refresh the Digitalline registration. Wait until the phone re-registers, then have your customer inform the callers to try dialing their number again.

Understanding the "Find Me" Status: "Answered - Not Accepted". "Answered - Not Accepted" indicates that the call has been forwarded and picked up by the callee, however BT Cloudphone did not recognize that the callee "accepted" the call by pressing "1". Pressing "1" is an option triggerred by enabling the "Incoming call information" feature called "Play announcement before connecting".
If BT Cloudphone is not detecting that the callee is pressing "1", this does not always mean that the callee's phone is at fault. Below are some of the common causes that will help identify why BT Cloudphone could not identify that the caller pressed "1" to accept the call.
  • DTMF codes not being recognized
    • There are times that DTMF codes are not being properly passed to BT Cloudphone causing us to "not detect" that the call was already accepted.
    • This can be caused by line quality issues as these codes are passed using distinct tones from one phone system to another. A simple break during the transmission could cause the listening party to not distinguish the code.
  • Call forwarding duration
    • There are instances when the callee is not being given an ample time to press "1" to accept the call.
    • The recommended "Ring for" duration is 20 to 30 seconds, so if the call forwarding rule is below the recommended values, have the customer increase it.

Understanding the "Find Me" Status: "Line busy". "Line busy" indicates that the forwarding number cannot be reached by BT Cloudphone because it is "busy". This does not always mean that the forwarding number is at fault. Below are some of the common causes that will help identify why call forwarding is not working.
  • Call identifiers
    • Call identifiers may cause problems to the carrier we are forwarding the calls to.
    • There are times that carriers reject the call identifier, generally not letting the call pass through their system.
  • Outbound routing issues
    • It is possible that the call is not being properly routed to the detination carrier because RingCentral's routing table needs to be updated.
  • Call waiting feature is not active
    • A forwarding number without call waiting will ring "busy" if it is in an active call and another call comes in.

  • Call Handling & Forwarding > Settings

fields.name: UnderstandingtheFindMeStatusTimeout
fields.fieldText:
Understanding the "Find Me" Status: "Time out". "Time out" generally indicates that the "Ring for" duration was exceeded without the callee answering the phone.
This does not always mean that the callee is at fault. Below are some of the common causes that will help identify why the callee did not get the chance to answer the call.
  • Call identifiers
    • Call identifiers may cause problems to the carrier we are forwarding the calls to.
    • There are times that carriers reject the call identifier, generally not letting the call pass through their system.
      • BTCloudphone may not identify that the call was rejected, causing the call forwarding process to timeout.
  • Post-dial delays and call forwarding duration
    • "Time out" happens when the "Ring for" duration has been exceeded while BT Cloudphone is still trying to "contact" the receiving party.
    • The recommended "Ring for" duration is 20 to 30 seconds.
    • Excessive delays when call forwarding begins can play a part why callers hangup. The delay happens when RingCentral is routing the call to the forwarding number.
      • Due to the delay, the call forwarding duration may expire while BT Cloudphone is still "connecting" to the forwarding number.
To isolate issues with call identifiers, check if the feature is enabled by going to:
  • Call Handling & Forwarding > Settings
  • Incoming Call Information > Displayed incoming caller ID > Edit
